executive_summary:
Del Taco is a Yadav Enterprises-owned, predominantly franchised Mexican QSR executing an 18-month post-acquisition turnaround called Project Sunrise. At fiscal year-end September 28, 2025, the inherited estate comprised 576 restaurants—132 company-operated and 444 franchised—with $918.8 million in systemwide sales. The operating baseline was pressured: system same-store sales declined 3.7%, company-store transactions declined 6.9%, and restaurant-level margin was 11.1%.

Yadav's leadership reset and Project Sunrise create an active transformation agenda centered on unit-level execution, cost optimization, consistent food quality, value, guest trust, and modernization of systems and processes. That agenda makes menu accuracy, promotional speed, restaurant consistency, franchisee economics, reliability, and measurable operational improvement the appropriate technology outcomes.

The technology environment remains a qualification issue. Qu announced a broad Del Taco modernization in 2024, while historical evidence also supports NCR/Aloha and MenuLink. Worldpay is the confirmed payments relationship; the contract extension was signed September 3, 2026 after an approximately nine-month process. Olo is carried at medium confidence. Presto must be treated as historical/discontinued unless new evidence establishes otherwise.

The September 8 call with Maggie Lenhart materially improved the access path. Maggie owns the Worldpay relationship, Todd owns the Genius expansion motion, and they agreed to operate as a coordinated team. Maggie has direct access to Daniel and reported access to Dean, Yadav's CIO and a Genius advisory-board member, and planned to request a joint discovery meeting. The broader Yadav thesis includes reported Square use at Nick the Greek and a Qu-related pilot whose exact scope and performance remain unverified.

The recommended posture is relationship-led and discovery-first. Lead with a Del Taco digital-menu-board and operational-execution discussion tied to Project Sunrise, validate the inherited POS and vendor estate, and use a successful Del Taco motion as a potential—but not assumed—path into the broader Yadav portfolio.
current_business_situation:
Del Taco entered Yadav Enterprises ownership on December 22, 2025 following a sale by Jack in the Box valued at approximately $119 million after customary adjustments. The inherited operating base comprised 576 restaurants at fiscal year-end 2025, with 444 franchised and 132 company-operated locations. Fiscal 2025 systemwide sales were $918.8 million, while system same-store sales declined 3.7%, company-store transactions declined 6.9%, and restaurant-level margin was 11.1%. Fourteen restaurants opened while 32 closed.

Management is executing Project Sunrise, an 18-month turnaround centered on restoring core food quality and consistency, simplifying operations where needed, strengthening value, rebuilding guest trust, accelerating executable menu innovation, expanding catering, and improving loyalty. The plan creates an operating mandate across marketing, R&D, operations, sourcing, franchise relations, and technology.

The Worldpay contract extension was signed September 3, 2026. This removes the renewal-period coordination constraint and creates a cleaner window for a joint Worldpay/Genius discovery motion, but it does not confirm a formal Del Taco sourcing event. Maggie Lenhart planned to approach Daniel for a joint discovery meeting; that meeting and the customer's priorities remain to be confirmed.
